title: WordsEnigma: a word game, end to end

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Word games look simple on the surface. Underneath, someone has to keep track of players, languages, word lists and every guess.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's built on Redwood, with separate web and API workspaces. The data model links users, languages, word banks, games and individual guesses.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And how does the front end talk to the database?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Through GraphQL services, which translate what the app wants to do into Prisma calls on the database. It's almost entirely TypeScript.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What does the game engine do?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The project describes a dictionary validator and a solver supporting multiple languages and word lengths. So it can check words and help find answers, not just record them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's a fork, with the upstream credited, and tested with Jest and Testing Library. The written page maps out how the pieces connect.
